name: Writer's Studio
tagline: Ideas, drafts, the book and the newsletter in one calm place, with writing tools, a style guide and editing passes built in.
description:
A home for a working writer, shown through a worked example: Nell Ashby, a fictional essayist who sends a fortnightly newsletter and is halfway through a book of essays about repair. Ideas land on the Desk, get promoted to pieces, and move through a pipeline from outline to published, with word counts, progress and the words a day each deadline needs.

Every piece is a real page: an outline, a draft excerpt and a scratch space for the messy bits, linked to the research behind it. The book has a corkboard of chapters by part and a tracker that shows how far the manuscript has come and when the first draft will land at your real pace. Pitches, guest essays and prize entries live in Submissions, with the pitch as sent and a count of the days you have been waiting.

Four tools sit where you would reach for them: a word sprint timer that keeps a Writing log, a prose check for readability, rhythm and echoes with a read-aloud test, a subject line preview for the newsletter, and the book tracker. Five AI recipes turn notes into an outline, write a reader's report, line-edit against your style guide, suggest headlines and draft pitches.
credits: Short public-domain quotations from Henry David Thoreau (Walden), John Ruskin (Unto This Last) and William Morris (The Beauty of Life). Everything else is original.
overview: Writing workspace: an ideas inbox, a pieces pipeline with word-count progress, a writing log, a book corkboard and tracker, submissions, a commonplace book and reading notes, a style guide, editing and publishing checklists, and outline templates.
